clue.text: Spaces under the bridge

parts.note: the bridge is the bony ridge of the nose, and the spaces beneath it are the two openings we breathe through, not gaps under a river crossing

explanation.surface: Someone describes the gaps below a river crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' suggests a river or road crossing; read it as the bridge of the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: The openings of the nose sit just below its bony ridge, called the bridge.

clue.text: it may pinch a young child

explanation.surface: A crab's claw nips a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that nips, such as a crab's claw, can be so named; and a small child, especially a boy, is informally a nipper.

clue.text: What cry, when suffering equals?

indicators.note: suffering suggests being knocked about, so the letters of equals are reordered

explanation.surface: Asks what noise people of equal rank make when in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffering' rearranges EQUALS; 'What' and 'when' are link words framing a question.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeal is a long high-pitched shriek, the kind of noise a hurt person or animal makes.

clue.text: Withdraw to a place for meditation

explanation.surface: Someone pulls back to a quiet spot to reflect.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull back from a position is to fall back; a quiet secluded refuge for prayer or reflection has the same name.

clue.text: Hair fastener?

explanation.surface: A slide or clip for keeping hair in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress or curl of hair is so called; so is the device on a door that secures it with a key.

clue.text: Man using plug with rain swirling about

parts.note: a plug is a piece of publicity, an advert, shortened to AD

indicators.note: swirling about says the letters of the word rain are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A man tries to stop leaks while rain swirls around him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' looks like a stopper for a drain in the rain; in crosswords it is a piece of publicity. 'Swirling about' is the anagram signal, and 'using' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrian is a male first name, and crosswords often define a name simply as a man.

clue.text: Thomas was determined to hide silly bet

indicators.note: to hide says one piece covers another, here DOUR wrapped around the jumbled letters

parts.note: dour means stern and obstinate, firmly determined

indicators.note: silly suggests nonsense, so the letters of bet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Thomas was set on concealing a foolish wager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' is the anagram signal and 'to hide' the container. 'Doubting Thomas' is the apostle who would not believe in the Resurrection without proof, so 'Thomas' is the definition, not a man's name in the story.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Thomas refused to believe without seeing proof, so his name stands for any sceptic.

clue.text: In the break see girl from Bury

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body in a grave
Val is a girl's name, short for Valerie

explanation.surface: During the half-time break, look at the girl from the town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the English town (it is in Greater Manchester); it is the verb. 'In the', 'see' and 'from' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a pause between parts of a performance or game.

clue.text: Fool starts to read out information on gas

parts.note: a nit, short for nitwit, is a fool

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letter of each of the words read and out

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A fool begins reading out facts about a gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is a link word. GEN is British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is the colourless, odourless gaseous element making up most of the air.

clue.text: Dressing couple in a struggle and holding it back

indicators.note: holding means one piece wraps around the other, here the rearranged couple around the turned word
something in a struggle is thrashing about, so the letters of couple are jumbled
back says the short word it is to be read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A pair wrestle with something and keep hold of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' suggests clothes or salad; it is a medical dressing. 'In a struggle' gives the anagram (POULCE), 'back' the turned word, and 'holding' sets it in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A poultice is a soft moist mass applied as a wound dressing, often warmed, to soothe or draw out infection.

clue.text: Either way it's a sign of mild disapproval

indicators.note: either way says the answer reads identically from left to right and from right to left

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A tutting noise expresses mild displeasure whichever way it is made.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads the same in both directions, which is all the wordplay there is.
explanation.definitionFit: Clicking the tongue twice is the conventional spoken signal of gentle reproach.

clue.text: Spend money frivolously on a piece of batter

explanation.surface: Wasting cash on a fried snack.
explanation.definitionFit: To fritter money away is to waste it; a fritter is also a slice of food dipped in batter and fried.

clue.text: Stationery item makes times table finally right

parts.note: times in the sense of periods of history are eras

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word table

explanation.surface: A schoolchild's times table, with the last answer made correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times table' reads as multiplication; it is TIMES (ERAS) then the last letter of 'table'. 'Makes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber for removing pencil marks is an item kept with pens and paper on a desk.

clue.text: Speaker I love on music

parts.note: a speaker who makes speeches is an orator
love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A speaker announces their love of music.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis 'love' is nil, which looks like O. 'On' is a link word: in an across clue the pieces simply follow on.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large-scale choral and orchestral composition on a sacred theme, such as Handel's Messiah.

clue.text: Boy with social worker attending ceremony

parts.note: a page is a boy servant or attendant
the ant is a social insect, a worker in its colony

explanation.surface: A boy accompanied by a social worker goes to a formal occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' reads as a care professional; it is the ant, a social insect. 'With' and 'attending' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a grand public show or procession, a ceremonial spectacle.

clue.text: Cavorting streaker at a first test is some cold dish!

indicators.note: cavorting means prancing about wildly, so the letters gathered are thrown into a new order
first picks the opening letter of the word test

explanation.surface: A naked fan leaps about the pitch on the opening day of a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cavorting' rearranges STREAKER, AT, A and T (the first letter of 'test'). A Test is an international cricket match, and streakers are pitch invaders who run on naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak tartare is raw minced beef served uncooked, typically with a raw egg yolk, so it is eaten cold.

clue.text: Wind starts to scatter one legendary highflyer's business

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letter of the word scatter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend
Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A wind begins to scatter the papers of a famous jet-setter's company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highflyer' suggests a successful person; it is the roc, the giant bird of the Arabian Nights.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot dust-laden wind blowing from North Africa across the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Purge sin with speed

parts.note: lust is one of the seven deadly sins
rate means speed, as in rate of travel

explanation.surface: Wiping out wickedness quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To lustrate is to purify ritually, cleansing by ceremony or sacrifice.

clue.text: A notable trial in Paris

parts.note: the French phrase for a famous case, a lawsuit that attracts wide attention, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A famous court case held in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Paris' signals that the answer is in French; the phrase is used in English too.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase literally means a celebrated case, a controversy or lawsuit that draws great public interest.

clue.text: Flights opponents take to headlands

parts.note: in bridge East and South are opposing partners, E and S
capes are headlands jutting out to sea

explanation.surface: Rival teams set off for the coastal cliffs.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, so any two neighbouring compass points are opponents. 'Take to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is an act of running away, and escapes are getaways.

clue.text: Table includes old bird

indicators.note: includes means one piece contains another, here the list holding the letter

parts.note: a roster is a table or list of duties

explanation.surface: A list of names includes an aged bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' looks like an adjective for the bird, but it gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male chicken, a cockerel.

clue.text: Part of speech to declare bishop head of diocese in

indicators.note: in says that letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: to aver is to state or declare firmly

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word diocese

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop must speak up within his diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of' takes D from 'diocese', and 'in' puts it inside AVER + B: A-D-VER-B. 'To' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb is a word class modifying verbs, such as quickly or soon.

clue.text: You might be late arriving in this car

definitions.text: You might be late arriving in this car

parts.words: You might be late arriving in this car
parts.note: late here means dead, not behind time, so this vehicle carries a deceased person to a funeral

explanation.surface: Someone warns that a slow vehicle could make you miss an appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' looks like 'unpunctual'; it means 'deceased', as in 'the late Mr Smith'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearse is the vehicle carrying a coffin to a funeral.

clue.text: Loath to talk about small return on tiny sum of money

annotationWithheld.why: Loath to talk about small return on tiny sum of money (8): RE (about) + CENT (tiny sum of money) fit, but nothing in 'small return' gives TI; a word such as 'it' seems lost from the printed clue, and no search found the original
annotationWithheld.clue: Loath to talk about small return on tiny sum of money

clue.text: Compose ode with fun for saucy dish

indicators.note: compose means put together or arrange, so the letters of ode and fun are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A poet is told to write a light-hearted verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compose' rearranges ODE and FUN; 'with' only joins them and 'for' is a link word. 'Saucy' looks like cheeky but means served in sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A fondue is a pot of melted cheese or hot sauce into which bread or meat is dipped at the table.

clue.text: What you might need to play golf? Lots of trees

definitions.text: What you might need to play golf?

explanation.surface: A golfer reaches for a club in a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood is a golf club with a large head for long shots; it is also a stretch of land covered with trees.

clue.text: Title holders eat noisily on Sunday

parts.note: to champ is to chew loudly, munching with the jaws
S is the abbreviation for Sunday, as in calendars

explanation.surface: Victorious champions celebrate by feasting loudly on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is a link word: in an across clue S simply follows CHAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Champs is a casual short form for champions, those who hold a sporting title.

clue.text: Robert de Niro finally mixed drink

indicators.note: mixed means blended or stirred, so all the gathered letters are shuffled together
finally takes the closing letter of each of the words de and Niro

explanation.surface: The actor Robert De Niro finally mixes himself a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' gives E and O, the last letters of 'de' and 'Niro'; 'mixed' rearranges them with ROBERT. The film star's name is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Root beer is a sweet fizzy soft drink flavoured with sassafras root, popular in North America.

clue.text: Port some passed out from right to left

indicators.note: from right to left says those letters are read backwards, the opposite way to normal reading
some says only part of the run of letters in the next words is wanted

explanation.surface: Some of the crowd fainted, one after another along a line.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'passed out' sit the letters ASSEDO; reading them right to left gives the Black Sea port.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major seaport on the Black Sea coast of Ukraine.

clue.text: Some mead — or a blend that's lovely

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A drinker praises a blend of honey wine and something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the end of 'mead' through 'or a' into 'blend'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something charming enough to be called lovely is delightful, worthy of being cherished.
